significance: An early nineteenth-century Bhadrakali shrine near Ponkunnam, run by a committee of the Vellala Mahasabha, known for its daily Guruthi pooja and the Panthirukulam guruthi held once every twelve years. It is a well-used stop for Sabarimala pilgrims, who are given free meals there.
story: The temple is said to have been founded on the instruction of the head of the Manakkattu Mana, who prescribed a Bhadrakali shrine to appease a yakshi released by a saint whose spirit was spreading disease.
